newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat futures end lower on Plains rains.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat futures end lower on Plains rains.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed lower on rainfall this week that was seen boosting crop prospects in several key U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat area, traders said.
Cash dealers said there had been significant rainfall overnight in parts of Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas and there were forecasts for more rain over the next couple of days.

Most traders discounted concern about forecasts for a dip in temperatures in northwest Kansas over the weekend, when lows of around 29 degrees Fahrenheit are anticipated. A drop to around 26 degrees F for several hours would be needed to harm the crop, cash dealers said.
But traders said the cold weather may have kept away aggressive new selling interest.
The May contract Friday gained 3-3/4 cents per bushel on the new crop July as end-user demand surfaced in late dealings.
"It broke to levels considered fair value and there was end-user demand supporting the May late," a trader said.
KCBT wheat futures closed three to eight cents per bushel lower, with May down three at $4.02. July was down 6-3/4 at $3.74-1/2.
KCBT wheat futures volume Friday totaled 39,820 contracts, above the 33,605 traded Thursday.
